environment.architecture: Timber-and-coral-stone buildings climbing the harbor bluffs in uneven terraces; salvaged old-kingdom masonry reused as foundation stone throughout the older quarters.
environment.activity: Dive crews hauling gear to the docks at dawn, guild criers reading the day's licensed sites, a constant traffic of handcarts moving salvage from harbor to market.
environment.sensory: Salt, tar, and drying kelp; the clatter of winches; gulls and the distant clang of the Drowned Bell marking the tide.
environment.lighting: Bright and glaring at midday off the water; oil-lamp lit and rowdy after dark, especially near the harbor.

curiosities.detail: Old-kingdom stonework is visible in half the building foundations, if you know to look for the archaic lettering.
Everyone in Port Calder has a story about someone who dove too deep and came back wrong, or didn't come back at all.

environment.architecture: A natural deepwater cove walled in by old breakwaters, half of them salvaged old-kingdom seawall stone.
environment.activity: Dive boats, salvage barges, and Concordat inspection skiffs crowd the water; crews load and unload from dawn to dusk.
environment.sensory: Rope and tar, brine, the groan of hulls against pilings.
environment.lighting: Open sky; lantern-strung at night along the seawall.

curiosities.detail: A section of old breakwater stone bears worn old-kingdom carvings, half-submerged at low tide.

environment.architecture: A blocky, well-kept stone hall facing the harbor, Concordat blue-and-gold banners over the door.
environment.activity: Queues of divers waiting on permits; clerks stamping manifests; a guard or two watching the line.
environment.sensory: Ink, wax seals, the murmur of paperwork disputes.

curiosities.detail: The public manifest board is missing several recent dive-site postings — quietly pulled, not officially cancelled.

environment.architecture: A sprawl of wooden piers, some newer construction, some visibly built on older stone pilings.
environment.activity: Dive crews prepping gear, dockhands haggling over cargo, licensed and unlicensed boats jockeying for berths.
environment.sensory: Wet rope, fish, low tide mud at the pier bases.

curiosities.detail: One unmarked pier at the far end sees regular traffic at odd hours — no Concordat flag, no manifest posted.

environment.architecture: A weathered two-story shack on stilts at the harbor mouth, signal flags and a tide-bell strung from the roof.
environment.activity: Tide and weather postings, berth assignments, incident reports.
environment.sensory: Damp wood, lamp oil, chalk dust from the tide-board.

curiosities.detail: The harbormaster logs every unusual find and current shift with more care than her pay grade requires — she's tracking something.

environment.architecture: A massive green-black bronze bell, old-kingdom make, raised from the reef decades ago and hung in a timber frame at the harbor mouth.
environment.activity: Rung on the hour by a rotating duty-watch; a minor local landmark and meeting point.
environment.sensory: A low, resonant tone that carries over the whole harbor; faint verdigris smell of old bronze.

curiosities.detail: The bell's old-kingdom inscription isn't a maker's mark — it's a warning, in a dialect none of Port Calder's scholars fully recognize.
The bell was cast as part of the original containment working. Ringing it in a specific pattern (unknown to the surface) can be felt below.
